findings.remaining_risk: Historical artifact must remain excluded from future capability baselines.
findings.summary: Genesis V1 acceptance was withdrawn and corrected to INVALID_CAMPAIGN.

findings.remaining_risk: Historical artifact must not be used as frozen-campaign or capability baseline evidence.
findings.summary: Genesis V2 was reclassified as protocol execution and protocol/capability separation evidence only.

findings.remaining_risk: Historical artifact must remain excluded from current protocol readiness.
findings.summary: Protocol Baseline V1 acceptance was withdrawn and corrected to INVALID_CAMPAIGN.

findings.remaining_risk: Search results still expose historical V2 targets, but current workflow acceptance selects V3 artifacts only.
findings.summary: Protocol Baseline V2 acceptance was withdrawn because freeze binding, artifact verification, schema validation, persistence, redaction, budget settlement and preflight evidence were incomplete.

findings.impact: A future live-provider configuration could overtrust a hostname if DNS resolution changes after allowlist validation.
findings.remaining_risk: Live-provider execution still requires explicit credentials and preflight; remediation blocks known hostname-only/private-range/rebinding boundary gaps before live execution.
findings.remediation: Resolve provider hostnames at execution time, reject private/link-local/loopback addresses except explicit local-development providers, and record resolved address evidence.
findings.summary: Provider host allowlisting is hostname-string based and does not resolve DNS to block rebinding or private-range targets for non-local provider endpoints.

findings.impact: A configured provider endpoint could redirect to a different host unless urllib behavior is constrained or revalidated.
findings.remaining_risk: Redirects are blocked by default. If future redirect support is introduced, every hop must re-run scheme, host allowlist and resolved-address validation.
findings.remediation: Install a redirect handler that blocks redirects by default or revalidates scheme, host allowlist and resolved address on every redirect.
findings.summary: Provider HTTP transport uses urllib default redirect behavior without an explicit post-redirect host allowlist check.

findings.impact: A future real-provider campaign could be attempted with incomplete authorization, ambiguous provider identity, stale cases, or insufficient evidence binding.
findings.remaining_risk: Real provider capability remains unverified until a separately authorized Batch 09B supplies credentials, passes preflight, executes the live campaign and produces scored evidence.
findings.remediation: Batch 09A adds fail-closed provider configuration validation, campaign authorization schema, frozen case manifest, evaluator protocol, threshold specification, semantic hash contract, dry-run/preflight modes and readiness gates.
findings.summary: Real-provider Genesis execution previously lacked a complete pre-execution readiness contract for configuration, authorization, case manifest, thresholds, semantic hashes and operator runbooks.

findings.impact: No real-provider capability baseline, supported domains, aggregate correctness, capability improvement, hosted staging readiness or production readiness can be claimed.
findings.remaining_risk: The Batch 09B no-authorization blocker is superseded by later Genesis V7 attempt-2 evidence. Real-provider capability remains unestablished because GCR-010 and GCR-011 remain open.
findings.remediation: Preserve the Genesis V6 HOLD artifact as historical evidence. Use the later Genesis V7 attempt-2 evidence for current real-provider execution state, while leaving capability evidence blocked by invalid structured outputs and non-diagnosable provider-response records.
findings.summary: Batch 09B could not attempt real-provider execution, but this historical blocker was superseded by Genesis V7 attempt 2, which had a source-bound authorization, passed canary, and executed all 24 provider cases before reaching current evidence blockers.

findings.impact: No Genesis V7 real-provider capability baseline, supported domains, aggregate correctness, capability improvement, hosted staging readiness or production readiness can be claimed.
findings.remaining_risk: The original failed-canary artifact remains historical evidence; attempt 2 supersedes it for current Genesis V7 status.
findings.remediation: Provide a new explicit authorization bound to an available official model, endpoint, case manifest and budgets; rerun preflight and a new canary before any 24-case baseline execution.
findings.summary: Batch 09C attempted the authorized OpenAI canary but the exact authorized model was unavailable for the request, so the 24-case baseline was not started.

findings.impact: No cases were completed or scored, no domains were supported, aggregate correctness is unavailable, and no real capability baseline can be claimed.
findings.remaining_risk: Real-provider capability remains unestablished until valid, scorable provider outputs are produced and thresholds are evaluated.
findings.remediation: Prepared a source-bound request contract with domain-specific required JSON fields and a larger visible-output cap that remains under the local USD 3.00 hard cap. A future authorized campaign must rerun the frozen baseline under a new campaign identity and produce schema-valid, scorable outputs.
findings.summary: Genesis V7 attempt 2 established OpenAI gpt-5.6-luna reachability and model identity, but all 24 baseline cases produced schema-invalid structured outputs under the frozen evaluator contract.

findings.impact: The committed Genesis V7 attempt-2 case records cannot be independently diagnosed because the artifacts preserve only response hashes and status metadata for provider outputs.
findings.remaining_risk: A future run must preserve redacted provider responses, finish reasons, provider request ID hashes, parser inputs, parser input hashes and audit references before any real capability baseline can be accepted or rejected.
findings.remediation: Strengthened the capability genesis artifact verifier to reject hash-only V7 provider evidence, missing V7 payload manifests and identical response-hash patterns across provider-attempted cases.
findings.summary: Genesis V7 attempt 2 case evidence is hash-only for provider responses: all 24 case records lack redacted response bodies, finish reasons, provider request ID hashes, parser inputs and audit references required for independent diagnosis.
